title: Observation of linear magnetoresistance and planar Hall effect in the Dirac semimetal PdTe
authors: Bhawana Mehra, Bibek Ranjan Satapathy, V S Abhishek, Reena, Ritu Gupta, Yogesh Singh, S. Chakraverty, Amit Vashist
abstract: PdTe is a Dirac semimetal that also exhibits superconductivity, providing an intriguing platform to explore topological superconductivity and unconventional magnetotransport phenomena. While the superconducting properties of PdTe have been extensively studied in recent years, the detailed magnetotransport phenomena have remained unexplored. Here, we present the first observation of linear magnetoresistance (LMR) and the planar Hall effect (PHE) in a high-quality single crystal of PdTe. We observe temperature-dependent unsaturated LMR in both in-plane ($B \parallel I$) and out-of-plane ($B \perp I$) configurations. The magnetoresistance (MR) shows a crossover from parabolic to linear dependence at the critical field Bc, and detailed analysis indicates that disorder-driven mobility fluctuations are the origin rather than the Abrikosov quantum-limit mechanism. Furthermore, prominent PHE has been observed by rotating the magnetic field within the plane of the sample. The detailed analysis of the field and temperature dependence of PHE-amplitude, along with the parametric plot, suggests that PHE originates predominantly from the anisotropic orbital magnetoresistance rather than the chiral anomaly. Our results demonstrate that although the Dirac point is close to the Fermi level, the observed LMR and PHE in the Dirac semimetal PdTe can be understood within a semiclassical transport framework, highlighting the importance of distinguishing between topological and conventional classical transport mechanisms in topological materials
summary: This work reports the first observation of linear magnetoresistance and the planar Hall effect in the Dirac semimetal PdTe. By analyzing the field and angle dependence of these effects, the authors conclude that both phenomena are best explained by conventional semiclassical transport mechanisms, specifically anisotropic orbital magnetoresistance, rather than exotic topological effects like the chiral anomaly.
main_problem: The study aims to investigate the magnetotransport phenomena, specifically linear magnetoresistance (LMR) and the planar Hall effect (PHE), in the Dirac semimetal PdTe, while distinguishing between topological and conventional classical transport mechanisms.
main_result: The observed LMR and PHE in PdTe can be understood within a semiclassical transport framework, suggesting that the effects originate predominantly from anisotropic orbital magnetoresistance rather than the chiral anomaly.
method: Magnetotransport measurements were performed on high-quality single crystals of PdTe, measuring resistivity ($ho$) as a function of magnetic field ($B$) and angle ($\phi$), and fitting the data using semiclassical Boltzmann expressions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a type-I Dirac semimetal, PdTe, which also exhibits superconductivity. Measurements involve analyzing the Hall resistivity ($ho_{xy}$), magnetoresistance (MR), and the angular dependence of resistivity ($ho_{PHE}^{xy}$ and $ho_{AMR}^{xx}$).
key_observables: Linear magnetoresistance (LMR), Planar Hall Effect (PHE), Anisotropic Magnetoresistance (AMR), and the crossover of MR from quadratic to linear dependence at a critical field ($B_c$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), Magnetic Field ($B$), Carrier densities ($n_e, n_h$), and Mobilities ($\mu_e, \mu_h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the PHE can be modeled by a semiclassical Boltzmann expression, and that the LMR crossover is governed by disorder-driven mobility fluctuations rather than quantum limit effects.
figures_summary: Figures show $ho(T)$ and carrier parameters, the crossover of MR from quadratic to linear dependence with $B$, and angular/field dependence plots for PHE and AMR, including parametric plots.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the material properties (superconductivity, carrier concentrations) and then systematically analyzes the MR, showing a crossover to linearity. Subsequently, it analyzes the PHE and AMR, using angular dependence and parametric plots to rule out the chiral anomaly in favor of anisotropic orbital magnetoresistance.
why_interesting: While the paper focuses on condensed matter transport, the rigorous distinction between topological predictions (like the chiral anomaly) and classical semiclassical transport mechanisms is a key theme in modern topological physics, which can inform the understanding of quantum phenomena in engineered systems.
